'''Gady Kozma''' ({{Langx|he|גדי קוזמא}}) is an Israeli mathematician. Kozma obtained his PhD in 2001 at the [[Tel Aviv University|University of Tel Aviv]] with [[Alexander Moiseevich Olevskii|Alexander&nbsp;Olevskii]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=148684}}</ref> He is a scientist at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science|Weizmann Institute]]. In 2005, he demonstrated the existence of the scaling limit value (that is, for increasingly finer lattices) of the ''[[loop-erased random walk]]'' in three dimensions and its invariance under rotations and dilations.<ref>{{cite journal
| last=Kozma | first=Gady
| title=The scaling limit of loop-erased random walk in three dimensions
| arxiv=math/0508344
| journal=Acta Mathematica
| volume=199
| issue=1
| pages=29–152
| date=2007
| doi=10.1007/s11511-007-0018-8 | doi-access=free}}</ref>

A loop-erased random walk consists of a random walk, whose loops, which form when it intersects itself, are removed. This was introduced to the study of self-avoiding random walk by [[Greg Lawler|Gregory Lawler]] in 1980,<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Lawler | first1=Gregory F. | authorlink1=Greg Lawler
| title=A self-avoiding random walk
| journal=Duke Mathematical Journal
| date=September 1980
| volume=47
| issue=3
| pages=655–693
| doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-80-04741-9}}</ref> but is an independent model in another universality class. In the two-dimensional case, conformal invariance was proved by Lawler, [[Oded Schramm]] and [[Wendelin Werner]] (with [[Schramm–Loewner evolution]]) in 2004.<ref>{{citation
| last1=Lawler | first1=Gregory F. | authorlink1=Greg Lawler
| last2=Schramm | first2=Oded | authorlink2=Oded Schramm
| last3=Werner | first3=Wendelin | authorlink3=Wendelin Werner
| title=Conformal invariance of planar loop-erased random walks and uniform spanning trees
| journal=Annals of Probability
| volume=32
| issue=1B
| date=2004
| pages=939–995
| arxiv=math.PR/0112234
| doi=10.1214/aop/1079021469 | doi-access=free}}</ref> The cases of four and more dimensions were treated by Lawler, the scale limiting value is Brownian motion, in four dimensions. Kozma treated the two-dimensional case in 2002 with a new method. In addition to probability theory, he also deals with Fourier series.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kozma|first1=Gady|last2=Olevskii|first2=Alexander|date=2006|title=Analytic representation of functions and a new quasi-analyticity threshold|journal=Annals of Mathematics |series=Second series |volume=164 |issue=3  |pages=1033–1064 |arxiv=math/0406261|bibcode=2004math......6261K |doi=10.4007/annals.2006.164.1033|s2cid=18052987}}</ref>

In 2008 he received the [[Erdős Prize]] and in 2010 the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]].  He is an editor of the ''[[Journal d'Analyse Mathématique]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://math.huji.ac.il/~w-jam/board.html|title=Editorial board|website=Journal d'Analyse Mathématique, homepage at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem|access-date=16 October 2022}}</ref>

In 2024 together with Shahaf Nitzan he published a reduction of [[Dying percolation conjecture|<math display="inline">\theta(p_c)=0</math> conjecture]] to various [[FKG inequality|correlation inequalities]] decreasing in strength<ref>{{cite Arxiv |last1=Kozma |first1=Gady |last2=Nitzan |first2=Shahaf |title=A reduction of the &theta;(p<sub>c</sub>) = 0 problem to a conjectured inequality |date=2024 |class=math.PR |eprint=2401.12397}}</ref>. They are supported by numerical evidence, and if true, any of them will resolve the conjecture.
